newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Chase Manhattan in Romania loan despite ruling.
newsitem.headline: Chase Manhattan in Romania loan despite ruling.

text.p: The Romanian branch of Chase Manhattan pledged on Wednesday to proceed with steps to arrange a $200 million loan for Romania's National Oil Company (CRP) to import crude oil despite a ruling suspending the CRP.
"Our initial reaction is that the ruling is not a serious obtstacle to our transaction," a bank official told Reuters.

On Tuesday, the Court of Appeal ruled to suspend the CRP after a local private firm, General Trading and Investments Co SA (GTI), filed a lawsuit accusing the state-run holding of monopolistic practices. GTI asked the court to annul the government decision last July to create the CRP.
"We are proceeding in our efforts to put together first class syndicate banks and we were very successful indeed, today," the official said without elaborating.
The $200 million credit would be used by CRP to finance vital crude oil imports during the coming winter.
Last winter, an acute shortage of hard currency cut Romania's oil imports. The Balkan country was forced to cut electricity supplies drastically to its main industries.
"There is a lot of market interest in this transaction. Romania requires the oil and also the financing," the Chase Manhattan official said.

GTI also complained that the CRP, a holding grouping 12 state-owned refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as an oil exploration company, had hindered its oil imports by blocking access to the country's sole oil port, Constanta on the Black Sea.

The CRP rejected the allegations and said it would appeal to the Supreme Court. It also said it would sue GTI over "slander, groundless accusations as well as material and moral damage caused the CRP on local and international markets."

"The ruling has no substance. The document published by GTI does not affect the activity of the CRP at all. The CRP was legally created and registered," general manager Mihail Georgescu told a news conference.
"We are not a monopoly. The CRP has no consolidated budget. All companies in the holding have their own budget and juridical status," he added.
The government says the CRP is intended to provide funds to import crude and streamline exploration, refining, distribution and transport of oil.
But some analysts see the new holding as on old-style East Bloc bureaucratic conglomerate.
